alt: A padlocked metal gate installed across the full width of a marked cycle path in Tower Hamlets, London, with cycle lane markings visible on the ground and the locked gate completely blocking access
story: In August 2026, Tower Hamlets council installed a full-width padlocked gate across a marked, heavily-used cycle path in London, with no alternative route and no key for cyclists — prompting widespread ridicule from residents who called it 'car-brained' planning; cyclists arriving at the gate are forced to turn back or lift their bikes around it, while a standard removable bollard would have blocked cars without stopping cyclists at all.
why_funny: The council chose the most bicycle-hostile possible solution to stop cars from entering a cycle path — accidentally converting an active cycle route into a dead-end.
